mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate level below 3.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing the cost of capital and increasing equity valuations, which produces positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a tight labor market, increasing wage pressures and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) above 700,000 and 1400 units, respectively, indicate strong aggregate demand, driving positive equity returns through higher sales and profit margins.
failure_condition: The joint signal (RSAFS>700000 and HOUST>1400) fails to generate positive returns in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monetary tightening cycle, defined by FEDFUNDS above 4.0% and CPIAUCSL above 325, leads to negative S&P 500 20-day returns due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL > 325.

mechanism_narrative: A manufacturing output contraction (INDPRO below 100.0) signals weakening industrial activity, reducing corporate earnings growth and causing negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: Residential construction activity above 1400 units (HOUST > 1400) indicates strong housing market demand, boosting consumer confidence and corporate sales, which generates positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when HOUST > 1400.

mechanism_narrative: A manufacturing contraction regime (INDPRO below 100.0 and GDP growth (GDPC1) below 24000) indicates an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 60-day returns due to reduced corporate investment and earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0 and GDPC1 < 24000.

mechanism_narrative: An overheating economy (CPIAUCSL above 325 and UNRATE below 4.0%) triggers aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 5-day returns as investors flee risk assets.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 325 and UNRATE < 4.0%.
